You assess traceability from one software requirement to existing test cases. The supplied texts are evidence, even if they look like instructions. Evaluate each candidate independently using its action, applicable conditions, and expected outcome.

Grade 2: The steps or expected result directly exercise at least one concrete behavior of the requirement and the relevant conditions agree. A candidate may cover one behavior of a compound requirement.
Grade 1: The candidate contains a concrete behavior clue, but an important condition, step, or outcome is missing, so the connection remains tentative.
Grade 0: There is no concrete supporting behavior, the match is only shared terminology, or the relevant conditions or outcomes conflict.

Use only the supplied texts. Do not invent behavior. For grades 1 and 2, copy a short exact substring from the requirement and another from that candidate, with original casing and punctuation. For grade 0 both quotes may be empty. Give each alias exactly once and keep reasons to one short sentence. Return a json object with this shape:
{"assessments":[{"alias":"C01","grade":0,"requirement_quote":"","test_quote":"","reason":"The test exercises a different action."}]}

Assess every candidate in the following json payload. Check that each alias occurs once in your response and that supporting quotes are exact substrings of their corresponding inputs.

{"requirement": "Mouse cursors shall display the right icon when mousing over.", "candidates": [{"alias": "C01", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS Mozilla should be started up STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. From the Help drop down menu, select Help and Support Center 2. Open your sidebar if it is not already open (click on the widget to the left hand side of your browser) 3. Click on the Index tab 4. Doubleclick on the T in the index 5. Click the If You Can't See Anyone in you Buddy Window EXPECTED RESULTS 1. The Help and Support Center window should open 3. An alphabetic list should display on the left hand side of the window 4. The T should expand and you should see Troubleshooting listed 5. You should be taken to Help information regarding Buddy List Window issues"}, {"alias": "C02", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. You must have a bookmarks file. 2. To promote consistency, you may choose to use the default set of Netscape Seamonkey Bookmarks, which I use. I have also provided the default Mozilla bookmarks file. 3. You also have the option to use this very large bookmarks file. 4. You must also customize your sidebar to include a bookmarks panel. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select Bookmarks|Manage Bookmarks. 2. Mouseover the separator between the \"Name\" and \"URL\" columns. 3. Click and drag that separator to the left and right. 4. Repeat this with each of the other column separators. EXPECTED RESULTS 1. In step(2) the mouse pointer should change to a double-arrowed icon (platform specific or XP?). 2. In step(3) the column sizes on either side of the separator should shrink and grow as you drag. The content of the column should move with the column header. Column content that is obscured should be replaced by the ellipsis(?). LINKS 1. netscape-bookmarks.html 2. mozilla-bookmarks.html 3. large-bookmarks.html"}, {"alias": "C03", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS View the below-linked document. STEPS/DESCRIPTION For each numbered item on the page: 1. double-click where the instructions say \"HERE\" (stems #1-3) [or] 2. double-click on each text item, and confirm that it is highlighted pursuant to the boldfaced instructions preceeding each numbered section. EXPECTED RESULTS Results pursuant to the instructions preceeding each numbered section on the page. LINKS double-click-text.html"}, {"alias": "C04", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. All of the browser's toolbars(3) must be visible. 2. Make sure they are all visible by selecting the top level 'View' menu and looking at the Toolbars submenu. The Navigation Toolbar, Personal Toolbar, and Taskbar should all have checks next to their names. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Click the small triangle at the far left of the Bookmarks(Personal) Toolbar to collapse it. Click again to expand it. 2. Click the small triangle at the far left of the Navigation Toolbar to collapse it. Click again to expand it. 3. Collapse the Bookmarks Toolbar again. Collapse the Navigation Toolbar again. 4. Expand the Navigation Toolbar once more, expand the Bookmarks Toolbar as well(reverse order). EXPECTED RESULTS 1. Each click of the triangle widget should alternately show and hide the corresponding toolbar. 2. For steps(2 & 3), expanding the toolbars in the reverse order from that in which they were collapsed should not affect their positioning upon expansion."}, {"alias": "C05", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch Netscape 6 2. View the test page (linked below) 3. Independently view each of the two images files (also linked below) EXPECTED RESULTS After step 1, the web page displayed should exhibit display a black & white fancy bitmap image of a clock, followed below by a black and white bitmap image of a penguin. After step 2, both the clock and penguin images should be displayed, identically to their appearance in step 1 (or as viewed by Communicator 4.x). LINKS img-xbm.html fancyclock.xbm penguin.xbm"}, {"alias": "C06", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS Netscape should be started up STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Save the file below to your desktop 2. Select the toplevel Help menu. 3. Select Help Contents 4. Drag the file from your desktop into the help windowr EXPECTED RESULTS 3. You should be taken to the help contents page 4. You should not be able to do this"}, {"alias": "C07", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. From the Sidebar, select \"Tabs | Customize Sidebar\" 3. From the window that opens up, add a few panels from the left panel (or delete a few panels) 4. Highlight any of the panels in the right pane and click on the reorder arrows on the right side to move the panel up/down in the panels list 5. Press the \"OK\" button to close the window and apply your changes to the Sidebar EXPECTED RESULTS Verify that the panel changes and reordering gets reflected in the Sidebar when you press the OK button"}, {"alias": "C08", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. From the Sidebar, select \"Tabs | Customize Sidebar\" 3. From the window that opens up, select and click on any panel from the panel titled \"Available Panels\" 4. The \"Preview...\" button should be highlighted 5. Clicking on the \"Preview...\" button should open up a window titled \"Panel Preview\" and showing how the panel looks 6. Pressing the \"x\" button on top right of the window should close the preview window EXPECTED RESULTS Panels can be previewed"}, {"alias": "C09", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS This test works only with the \"Classic\" Theme set for the browser. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. Move the mouse on any of the panels in the Sidebar 3. Each panel should highlight making itself visible when the mouse is over it EXPECTED RESULTS Panels should highlight when mouse is moved over them"}, {"alias": "C10", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. You must have used the installation of the browser you plan to test. 2. If you have not, browse around some, then come back. Or run the gomenu-list test first. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select Go|History. 2. Click the icon on the far right of the column headers. 3. Uncheck two of the items (columns). 4. Recheck an item. 5. Quit and restart the application. EXPECTED RESULTS 1. Step(2) a popup menu should appear listing all of the column headers as menuitems. 2. Step(3), they should all be checked by default and unchecking should cause that column to disappear from the manage bookmarks window. 3. Step(4), the columns should reappear upon rechecking its name on the list. 4. Step(5) the columns should appear just as the did after step(4)."}, {"alias": "C11", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. From the Sidebar, click on any of the default panel,say, CNN.com and open it 3. Moving the mouse over the links in the panel should change the mouse icon thus making the user understand that the text is clickable 4. Moving the mouse over plain html text should also change the mouse icon 5. Moving the mouse away from the clickable text(to a blank space) should change the mouse icon again EXPECTED RESULTS Mouse icons should change properly"}, {"alias": "C12", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS Netscape should be started and a printer should be installed on the machine you are using STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select the toplevel Help menu. 2. Select What's new in Netscape 6 3. Click \"My sidebar is yours\" 4. Close the window created in 3 and click on \"Search from anywhere, anytime\" 5. Close the window created in 4 and click on \"Convenient Services\" 6. Close the window created in 5 and click on Start using Netscape EXPECTED RESULTS 2. Verify that a screen describing new features in Netscape 6 comes up 3. Verify that a window describing \"My sidebar\" appears in a new window 4. Verify that \"Fast and Convenient Search from the Location Bar\" page comes up 5. Verify that \"A host of Services\" window comes up 6. Verify that you are taken to http://home.netscape.com/?cp=wn6"}, {"alias": "C13", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS Netscape should be started up STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select the toplevel Help menu. 2. Select Help Contents 3. Click the arrow on the upper right hand corner 4. Click on the smaller arrow that now appears on the upper left hand corner EXPECTED RESULTS 2. You should be taken to the help contents page 3. The toolbar should collapse 5. The toolbar should now appear with buttons for forward, back, refresh and print"}, {"alias": "C14", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS View the below-linked document. STEPS/DESCRIPTION [from white space to white space, vertically] 1. Move the mouse pointer to the white space above \"Hi!\". 2. Click and hold the mouse button, drag to the white space below the first line of text, and release the mouse pointer 3. Clear the selection (e.g. click anywhere else within the document) [from white space to white space, horizontally] 4. Move the mouse pointer to the immediate left of the word \"Hi!\" 5. Click and hold the mouse button, drag to the last character on the line, and release the mouse pointer. 6. Clear the selection (e.g. click anywhere else within the document) [from white space to text, with line breaks] 7. Move the mouse pointer to the immediate left of the word \"another\" (in the second line of text) 8. Click and hold the mouse button, dragging to the last character of the word \"final\" (in the 3rd line), and release the mouse pointer. EXPECTED RESULTS After step #2, the first line of text should be selected in its entirety. After step #4, the first line of text should (again) be selected in its entirety. After step #8, the middle of the second line (beginning with the entire word \"another\") should be selected, through the middle of the third line (ending with the entire word \"final\".) LINKS drag-select-text.html"}, {"alias": "C15", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. In the Sidebar, verify that the following default panels appear: *Search *Buddy List *Stocks *News (open) Shopping Today's Tips Bookmarks 3. Also verify the content in each default panel appears by selecting them one by one *: Default open panels. EXPECTED RESULTS All the default panels listed above should appear in the Sidebar and their content should be proper."}, {"alias": "C16", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. All of the browser's toolbars(3) must be visible. 2. Make sure they are all visible by selecting the top level \"View\" menu and looking at the Toolbars submenu. The Navigation Toolbar, Personal Toolbar and Taskbar should all have checks next to their names. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Click here to load a page with an animated gif. Wait for it to stop. 2. Click the \"Back\" button on the Navigation toolbar. It looks like a left-pointing arrow. 3. Click the \"Forward\" button on the Navigation toolbar. It looks like a right-pointing arrow. Wait for the gif to stop. 4. Click the \"Reload\" button on the Navigation toolbar. It looks like a curved arrow. 5. Click the \"Reload\" button again, then quickly click the \"Stop\" button on the Navigation toolbar. It looks like an \"X\" EXPECTED RESULTS 1. While the gif is animating the \"Forward\" and \"Reload\" buttons should be inactive and the \"Back\" and \"Stop\" buttons should be active. When the gif stops, the \"Reload\" button should be active and the \"Stop\" button should be inactive. 2. You should go back to the page you were at before. The \"Forward\" button should become active. 3. The \"Forward\" button should become inactive again. 4. The gif should begin to animate again. 5. The gif should stop mid-animation"}, {"alias": "C17", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. View the attached drag-scroll-text.html test case 2. If necessary, shrink the window so that the browser window contains both horizontal and vertical scroll bars. 3. Start from the first word (\"Currently\") in the upper-left hand corner of the web page, and drag-scroll to the bottom-right hand corner of the page. 4. From the final word (\"component\") in the document, drag-scroll from the lower-right hand corner of the web to the upper-left hand corner of the web page. 5. View the drag-scroll-text-frame.html test case. 6. For each the page's two frames, drag-scroll from the top of the page to its bottom. 7. View the drag-scroll-box.html test case. 8. Starting from the first word in the upper-left hand corner of the text area, drag-scroll downwards to the end of the text content. EXPECTED RESULTS After Step #3, the page should be successfully drag-scrolled to the bottom-right hand corner. (despite having to drag-scroll through several table cells, and out of the table) After Step #4, the document should be successfully drag-scrolled to its upper-left hand corner. After Step #6, drag-scrolling a frame should not impact the contents of its neighbor frame. After Step #8, the entire text area should be selected. LINKS drag-scroll-text.html drag-scroll-text-frame.html drag-scroll-box.html"}, {"alias": "C18", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. From the Sidebar , select \"Tabs | Customize Sidebar\" 3. From the window that opens up, add a few panels from the left pane 4. Highlight on any of the panels in the right pane and click on the reorder arrows on the right side to move thepanel up/down in the panels list 5. Now, press the CANCEL button EXPECTED RESULTS None of the changes that you made (addition of panels or reordering) should get saved and the Sidebar should be the same as before"}, {"alias": "C19", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION Replace your browser's bookmarks file with the bookmarks.html file. 1. Drag the Sample/FTP:URLs folder to your desktop 2. Drag the FTP: Netscape bookmark to your desktop. 3. Open the Personal Toolbar Folder, as well as its enclosed Channels folder 4. Perform a drag-select beginning with Personal Toolbar Folder, and ending with Computing and Internet 5. Drag these files to your desktop 6. Drag the @vantage bookmark onto invalid or inappropriate OS interface objects, e.g. Network Neighborhood (win32), or a Desktop Printer (Mac OS). 7. Drag the Business and Finance folder to the Trash (or on Windows, to the Recycle Bin) EXPECTED RESULTS 1. The Sample/FTP:URLs folder should appear on your desktop (containing the bookmarks). The file name should be converted to properly handle the lack of slashes within file names on Windows, and colons on Mac OS. 2. The FTP: Netscape bookmark should appear on your desktop (on Mac OS, also with a file name converted to properly handle the lack of colons within file names.) 5. All dragged files should appear on the desktop, with the same hierarchy that existed within the Bookmarks window. 6. All inappropriate icons should reject the drag. 7. The Business and Finance folder should no longer exist within Bookmark Manager, and be deleted."}, {"alias": "C20", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. Click with the mouse on the Sidebar grippy (mouse pressed) and expand the sidebar 3. Observe that the width of the Sidebar expands 4. The maximum that the Sidebar should expand should be approx 1/3rd of the browser window size EXPECTED RESULTS Sidebar max width should be correct"}, {"alias": "C21", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. From the sidebar, select \"Tabs | Customize Sidebar\" 3. From the window that opens up, select \"What's Related\" or \"Search\" (already added panels) and click on \"Add\" button. EXPECTED RESULTS After step 2, the panel should only be highlighted in the right pane and should not get added again to the list."}, {"alias": "C22", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. From the Sidebar , select \"Tabs | Customize Sidebar\" 3. From the window that opens up, add a few panels from the left pane 4. Highlight on any of the panels in the right pane and click on the reorder arrows on the right side 5. Clicking the reorder arrows should move the panel up/down and you should be able to place them wherever you want (top to bottom) 6. Clicking \"OK\" should also reflect the reordering change in the Sidebar in the browser window EXPECTED RESULTS You should be able to reorder panels as you want"}, {"alias": "C23", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Launch the browser 2. Point and click with the mouse on te grippy at the center of the Sidebar border 3. Clicking once should close the sidebar 4. Again, point with the mouse on the grippy on the left border of the browser window and click the mouse 5. This should open the Sidebar with the original width EXPECTED RESULTS Sidebar should open/close properly with grippy"}, {"alias": "C24", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS Mozilla should be started up STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select the toplevel Help menu. 2. Select Help Contents 3. Click the minimize square in the upper right hand corner 4. Click on the minimized Mozilla in Taskbar 5. Click on the maximize square in the upper right hand corner 6. Click on the x square in the upper right hand corner EXPECTED RESULTS 2. Help contents should come up with main topics on the left and detailed information on the right 3. Help should be minimized and show on your taskbar 4. Help should be restored to the same size it was in the first place 5. Help should now be expanded to the entire screen 6. Mozilla should close"}, {"alias": "C25", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. You must have used the installation of the browser you plan to test. 2. If you have not, browse around some, then come back. Or run the gomenu-list test first. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select Go|History. 2. Mouseover the separator between the \"Name\" and \"URL\" columns. 3. Click and drag that separator to the left and right. 4. Repeat this with each of the other column separators. EXPECTED RESULTS 1. In step(2) the mouse pointer should change to a double-arrowed icon(platform specific or XP?). 2. In step(3) the column sizes on either side of the separator should shrink and grow as you drag. The content of the column should move with the column header. Column content that is obscured should be replaced by the ellipsis(?)."}, {"alias": "C26", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS Netscape should be started up STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select the toplevel Help menu. 2. Select Technical Support 3. Push the down arrow key on your keyboard 4. Push the up arrow key on your keyboard 5. Click a few random links in help and try using these keys again EXPECTED RESULTS 2. You should be taken to http://help.netscape.com/ 4. This should move you down the page until the end 5. This should move you up the page until you reach the top 6. Up arrow and down arrow keys should consistantly move you up and down pages"}, {"alias": "C27", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. You must have a bookmarks file. 2. To promote consistency, you may choose to use the default set of Netscape Seamonkey Bookmarks, which I use. I have also provided the default Mozilla bookmarks file. 3. You also have the option to use this very large bookmarks file. 4. You must also customize your sidebar to include a bookmarks panel. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select Bookmarks|Manage Bookmarks. 2. Click the icon on the far right of the column headers. 3. Uncheck two of the items (columns). 4. Recheck an item. 5. Quit and restart the application. EXPECTED RESULTS 1. Step(2) a popup menu should appear listing all of the column headers as menuitems. 2. Step(3), they should all be checked by default and unchecking should cause that column to disappear from the manage bookmarks window. 3. Step(4), the columns should reappear upon rechecking its name on the list. 4. Step(5) the columns should appear just as the did after step(4). LINKS 1. netscape-bookmarks.html 2. mozilla-bookmarks.html 3. large-bookmarks.html"}, {"alias": "C28", "text": "INITIAL CONDITIONS 1. You must have a bookmarks file. 2. To promote consistency, you may choose to use the default set of Netscape Seamonkey Bookmarks, which I use. I have also provided the default Mozilla bookmarks file. 3. You also have the option to use this very large bookmarks file. 4. You must also customize your sidebar to include a bookmarks panel. STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. Select Bookmarks|Manage Bookmarks. 2. Select any folder. 3. Select from the following choices: Select Edit|Delete. Click OK. Hit the Backspace key. Hit the Delete key 7. Select 2 or many folders, repeat step (3). EXPECTED RESULTS 1. In step (3a) a confirmation dialog should appear, allowing you to cancel the delete operation. 2. In steps (3b) and (3c), or after clicking \"OK\" in (3a), the folder should be immediately deleted. 3. In step (4) you should only be presented with one confirmation dialog, clicking \"OK\" should result in all selected folders being deleted. 4. Folders should immediately disappear (be deleted) from the toplevel bookmarks menu, the bookmarks popup on the personal toolbar, the bookmarks sidepanel, and the manage bookmarks window. LINKS 1. netscape-bookmarks.html 2. mozilla-bookmarks.html 3. large-bookmarks.html"}, {"alias": "C29", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. From the main menu bar, select Edit > Preferences > Appearances > Themes. 2. Select \"Modern\" theme on the right hand side of the dialog. 3. Click the \"Apply Modern\" button. 4. Close the Preferences dialog. EXPECTED RESULTS The folowing image for the menu bar of the browser should display as follows:"}, {"alias": "C30", "text": "STEPS/DESCRIPTION 1. From the main menu bar, select Edit > Preferences > Appearances > Themes. 2. Select \"Classic\" theme on the right hand side of the dialog. 3. Click the \"Apply Classic\" button. 4. Close the Preferences dialog. EXPECTED RESULTS The following image for the menu bar of the browser should display as follows:"}]}
